messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Region eu-west-1 experiencing routing spillover to edge-tier. Error rate spike 5xx >= 4.8% over 5m window. Auto-fallback triggered to compatible model variant m-small-v2. Paging ops-oncall.
ops-oncall: Ack. Pulling up runbook and traces. ETA 2m. @tara.k you around?
tara.k: here. seeing increased 502s from router-proxy in eu-west-1, connections timed out to dedicated pool. Logs coming in.
mike.r: I can join for telemetry and routing policy. adding myself.
ops-oncall: Quick customer impact: tracing shows a subset of sessions got routed to us-east due to region capacity guardrail, some requests hit m-small-v2 causing degradation in latency and a mismatch in compatibility (structured outputs). Confirmed a handful of enterprise customers saw elevated error rates.
leah: Which fallback path was chosen? policy service should prefer same-region fallbacks first.
sahil: Fallback chosen: m-small-v2 (quantized) in us-east-1 via cross-region routing policy #3. Policy evaluation shows cost-tier priority overrid due to node pressure in eu-west-1.
ops-oncall: Live mitigation steps: 1) Hold new cross-region spillovers (disable policy-3 priority) 2) Gradually scale dedicated eu-west pool 3) Force-roll back some sessions to warm cache model variant m-base-full in eu-west (if capacity allows). Initiating step 1 now.
incident-bot: runbook:playbook-activate by ops-oncall at 2024-06-14T15:42Z.
ops-oncall: I flipped policy-3 to manual for the moment. Monitoring.
tara.k: attaching relevant log snippets:
```
[2024-06-14T15:39:21Z] router-proxy[euw-12] WARN conn_timeout user=acct_42 path=/v1/generate status=504
[2024-06-14T15:39:23Z] routing-mgr TRACE spillover decision: target=us-east-1 reason=pool_pressure nodes_idle=2/16
[2024-06-14T15:40:05Z] model-compat WARN output_schema_mismatch request_id=aa3e client=enterprise-x
```
mike.r: grabbing packet captures and perf counters from egress gateways. linking pcaps: https://internal.redwood/example-pcaps/1732048123
leah: Customer impact assessment in-flight: two named customers (AcmeCorp, Finlytics) had >30% error increase for 10-14 minutes. Ops to file SOC notification?
ops-oncall: Yes, I'm drafting a status for SRE->CS relay. Will include timeline and mitigations.
sahil: Hypotheses to track (in-thread): H1: abrupt node drain in eu-west-1 caused pool pressure causing policy-3 to prefer cross-region fallback. H2: policy-3 evaluation bug mis-ranked compatibility score (preferring quantized variant). H3: transient network flapping between router-proxy and model-serving causing timed-out cones.
ops-oncall: Good. We'll assign owners: H1 -> infra-bot + tara.k for pool diagnostics, H2 -> mike.r for policy logic/metrics, H3 -> leah for network traces.
infra-bot: Running node health sweep in eu-west-1 (job id sweep-1732048123). Reporting back in 3m.
ops-oncall: Meanwhile, temporary mitigation: pin AcmeCorp to eu-west-1 explicit routing via per-customer routing override. Deploying override for two customers now.
leah: Observed circuit resets on the local VPC edge at 15:39:18Z. Posting condensed tcpdump snippet:
```
15:39:17.982 SYN from router-proxy->model-node seq=0 win=64240
15:39:18.011 RST from model-node->router-proxy
15:39:19.004 SYN retransmit
```
tara.k: infra-bot result: 3 nodes out of 16 in eu-west-1 had degraded GPU heartbeats and were marked draining due to recent maintenance window. That reduced capacity below spill_threshold.
ops-oncall: So H1 confirmed as proximate cause for capacity pressure. Need RCA on why maintenance impacted live pool without reducing drain thresholds.
mike.r: I instrumented policy scoring logs, and there's a gap: compatibility_score computed as 0.71 for m-base-full vs 0.72 for m-small-v2 (quantized) because latency_estimate favored small-v2 due to historic metrics. Might be acceptable but we should review scoring weights.
sahil: For H2, adding note: scoring uses quantized_compat_penalty which may be underweighted.
ops-oncall: Next actions (live): A) continue scaling eu-west pool B) revert policy-3 automated priority until we tune scores C) open urgent change to maintenance procedures to exclude live-serving nodes or adjust draining thresholds D) post customer status and ETA.
ops-oncall: Scaling request submitted to autoscaler: scale-to 20 nodes (from 13). ETA 3m.
leah: After scale started, error rate dropped from 4.8% to 0.9% over 6 minutes. Latency slowly recovering.
ops-oncall: Good. Drafted customer note for CS: "We're seeing partial errors in eu-west-1 between 15:39-15:53 UTC caused by reduced serving capacity during maintenance which triggered cross-region spillover. We have reduced spillovers and scaled capacity; most traffic recovered. Investigating policy scoring and maintenance safeguards; follow-up RCA to be posted"
incident-bot: page created: incident/1732048123, severity: P2, owner: ops-oncall.
ops-oncall: For RCA coordination: let's collect full timelines, all logs, policy-eval traces, autoscaler events, maintenance tickets. I've created a shared doc: https://internal.redwood/docs/incident-1732048123 (will populate).
tara.k: I'll export kube events and node drain logs and drop them in the doc.
mike.r: I'll include policy-eval logs and the small script I used to recompute compatibility_score locally. snippet:
```
# quick eval
python tools/policy_eval.py --model m-base-full --variant m-small-v2 --sample-requests 1000
```
sahil: Suggest add a regression test that simulates a 3-node drain and ensures policy doesn't prefer quantized fallback for structured-output contracts.
leah: Agreed. Also request: add an alert when scheduled maintenance drains reduce serving capacity below spill_threshold (preflight check).
ops-oncall: Putting tasks in the incident doc. Owners: maintenance-preflight -> infra team, scoring-tune -> mike.r, regression-test -> devex.
ops-oncall: Any other immediate notes?
mike.r: One oddity: some requests that arrived after failover resumed were still routed to m-small-v2 for ~30s due to stale routing cache. We should add TTL reduction for routing cache during rollbacks.
tara.k: Noted.
ops-oncall: Closing live mitigation. We'll transition to post-incident RCA channel for writing. Leaving thread for any final logs. Thanks everyone. :heavy_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident moved to postmortems queue.
